definitions: A transaction that spans multiple distinct network hosts or servers, requiring all participating systems to either commit or abort the transaction together to maintain data consistency.
A set of operations that are performed across several independent systems, all of which must succeed or fail as a single atomic unit.
examples: Ensuring atomicity in a distributed transaction is crucial.
The two-phase commit protocol is often used for managing a distributed transaction.
Failures can be complex to handle in a distributed transaction.
